Background: This series contains Direct Normal Irradiance for the Interim Valley Monitoring Site, located in The Verdant Delta, The Commonwealth of Solis Island.
The Direct Normal Irradiance is the total amount of sun energy (in Watts per squared meter) arriving directly from the sun on a surface perpendicular to the sunlight direction. When there are no clouds to block the sun, the Direct Normal Irradiance is mostly a function of the position of the sun in the sky, with only small variations from factors such as water vapour and dust particles levels. Since it only measures the sun light coming straight from the sun, any light which gets scattered by clouds will not be measured. Therefore, cloudy weather conditions will reduce the Direct Normal Irradiance measurements, and clear weather conditions will see them at their highest possible values.

1. Executive Summary

This brief outlines the optical and mechanical design requirements for specialized solar sensors deployed within the Commonwealth of Solis Island, specifically for use at the Interim Valley Monitoring Site in The Verdant Delta. The objective of these specifications is to ensure the precision of Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI) measurements by strictly controlling the angular acceptance of incoming solar radiation.

To achieve high-fidelity data collection, these specialized solar sensors are designed with a narrow circumsolar limit field of view.
